readiness.evidencePolicy: Generated documents and asserted decisions are design evidence only. Schema validation, mock tests, account plans and deployed-system tests require separate receipts tied to the exact configuration. This export does not ingest implementation evidence.

requirements.statement: Accept PDF invoice uploads and durably queue extraction of supplier, invoice date, total and currency for staff review. Proposed safeguards retain source evidence and expose invalid, uncertain or failed extraction for correction without accounting submission.
requirements.rationale: Makes extraction useful and inspectable while preventing uncertain or invalid model output from silently progressing.
requirements.basis: “Users upload PDF invoices. Extract the supplier, invoice date, total and currency into a review queue.” Source evidence and explicit failure states are proposed safeguards.

requirements.statement: Require an authorized reviewer’s approval of the exact invoice result revision before accounting submission. Editing the approved fields invalidates that approval; extraction output and uploader-supplied claims cannot authorize delivery.
requirements.rationale: Prevents automated or stale approvals from authorizing accounting changes.
requirements.basis: “A reviewer approves a result before it is sent to our existing accounting API.” Revision binding and server-side reviewer authorization are proposed enforcement choices.

requirements.statement: Repeated intake delivery and processing or accounting retries must not create duplicate invoices. Persist intake and delivery identities, preserve the same operation and payload identity on replay, and hold uncertain accounting outcomes for reconciliation. Acceptance must include duplicate delivery, worker restart and timeout-after-destination-commit cases.
requirements.rationale: Repeated delivery and lost accounting responses can otherwise create duplicate financial records. End-to-end assurance depends on the destination’s independently tested idempotency and reconciliation behavior.
requirements.basis: “Delivery can repeat; retries must not create duplicate invoices.” Durable operation identity, bounded retries and uncertain-outcome reconciliation are proposed engineering controls.

requirements.statement: Keep invoice documents and extracted data within Australia during processing, model inference, storage, backups, recovery and accounting delivery, including logs containing invoice data. Explicitly flag unverified service/model availability and processing geography; require evidence before enabling affected paths, with no automatic overseas fallback.
requirements.rationale: Prevents invoice content from leaving Australia through inference, retained copies or the existing accounting destination. Regional labels alone do not establish compliance; destination evidence is required.
requirements.basis: User: “Keep documents and extracted data in Australia; flag unverified service availability.” Applies to invoice-workflow and accounting-api.

requirements.statement: Retain invoice originals and extraction audit history for 90 days. Implement and document cleanup across primary storage, object versions and database backups, including how restored data is re-expired. Demonstrate the effective retention behavior; do not claim that a 90-day eligibility setting alone meets this requirement.
requirements.rationale: Preserves the requested retention period while exposing the difference between cleanup eligibility and deletion across versions and backups; the proposed module needs evidence for the complete lifecycle.
requirements.basis: “Keep originals and extraction audit history for 90 days.” The invoice-workflow component owns storage, audit and cleanup.

requirements.statement: Support approximately 500 PDF uploads per day and bursts of twenty, with durable job status while processing takes several minutes. Acceptance must exercise the burst with bounded workers, persistent backlog and continued status access. No completion-time guarantee is inferred.
requirements.rationale: Durable asynchronous processing accommodates jobs lasting minutes and upload bursts without tying job survival to a browser connection.
requirements.basis: “500 uploads per day, bursts of twenty. Jobs may take several minutes.”

requirements.statement: Proposed safeguards: enforce authenticated, authorized access to invoice originals, extracted fields and audit history; protect transport and stored data; exclude invoice content and credentials from routine operational logs. Keep parser, model, database and accounting permissions separated and test denied access paths.
requirements.rationale: Personal data in originals and extracted evidence needs protection across application access, processing and operational records. These controls are engineering proposals, not asserted company policy.
requirements.basis: “they may contain personal data.” The existing diagram includes original storage, extraction, review and accounting delivery.

requirements.statement: Reference the existing accounting API without provisioning or modifying it. Accept endpoint and credentials through a secure administrator-controlled destination configuration. Qualify its adapter, authorization, residency, durable idempotency and reconciliation behavior before enabling delivery.
requirements.rationale: Preserves the existing accounting boundary and prevents a generated adapter contract from being mistaken for proven vendor compatibility.
requirements.basis: “The accounting system already exists. An administrator will supply its endpoint and credentials; treat it as external, not a new system to provision.”
